mainTopic: Calendar calculation and witnesses: the מולד, the hidden moon, the night-and-day rule for ראש חודש, and where a day of doubt goes
overview: The amud opens by finishing an earlier answer: pressuring witnesses so that ראש חודש is delayed would look like a lie, but setting it a day early would not. Next, שמואל claims he can fix the calendar for the whole גולה by calculation. אבא אבוה דרבי שמלאי tests him with a line from סוד העיבור about a מולד before or after חצות. שמואל admits he does not know it, so his claim is pushed back. רבי זירא then sends a message from ארץ ישראל explaining that line. Both the night and the day of ראש חודש must belong to the new month. A מולד before midday means the moon will be seen near sunset, and a מולד after midday means it will not. רב אשי explains that this rule, like רב נחמן's rule that the moon is hidden for twenty-four hours, is used to catch false witnesses. The גמרא then gives two sources for the night-and-day rule, from רבי יוחנן and from ריש לקיש. אביי and רבא disagree about whether those two sources lead to different results. Finally, רב נחמן teaches that a day kept out of calendar doubt is pushed forward, and the גמרא challenges why the 14th is not kept too.

steps.title: One move looks like a lie, the other does not
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא finishes an answer from the earlier discussion. Holding back testimony so that ראש חודש is delayed looks like a lie. Testifying so that ראש חודש comes earlier does not.
steps.simpleTranslation: This case looks like a lie. That case does not look like a lie.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is giving the last line of an answer to the earlier question about pressuring עדים. It explains why one kind of pressure is allowed and the other is not.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If עדים saw the moon but are told to keep quiet, ראש חודש gets pushed off. Other people may also have seen the moon, so the delay looks false. If ראש חודש is set a day early, no one is surprised, because everyone knows that only a few people may have seen the new moon.
steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that בית דין cared about how its rulings looked to the public. It would not do something that seemed obviously false, even when it was allowed to apply pressure.

phrases.notes: "This" means holding back testimony, so that ראש חודש is pushed off to the next day.

phrases.english: that does not look like a lie.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes the answer to the question from the previous section about pressuring witnesses.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Distinction between the two cases, based on how each one looks to the public
steps.terutzHavaAmina: One might think that both kinds of pressure on witnesses should be treated the same.
steps.terutzMaskana: Delaying ראש חודש looks like a lie and is not done. Making it earlier does not look like a lie.

steps.title: שמואל claims he can fix the calendar for the whole diaspora
steps.stepSummary: שמואל says he is able to set the calendar for the entire גולה through his own calculations.
steps.simpleTranslation: שמואל said: I am able to fix the calendar for the whole diaspora.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts a new topic with a bold claim from שמואל. He says his calendar knowledge is good enough to set the months for all the Jews outside ארץ ישראל.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Normally the calendar was set by בית דין in ארץ ישראל, based on עדים who saw the new moon. שמואל is saying that calculation alone could do the job. The next steps will test whether this claim holds up.

keyTerms.meaning: To fix / to arrange (here, the calendar)
The diaspora, the Jews living outside ארץ ישראל

phrases.english: I am able to fix (the calendar) for the entire diaspora.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר שְׁמוּאֵל: יָכֵילְנָא לְתַקּוֹנֵי לְכוּלַּהּ גּוֹלָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic: fixing the calendar by calculation instead of by witnesses.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: שמואל claims that he can set the calendar for the entire גולה by his own calculations.

steps.title: אבא tests שמואל with a puzzling line from a ברייתא
steps.stepSummary: אבא אבוה דרבי שמלאי asks שמואל whether he understands a line taught in סוד העיבור: a מולד before חצות versus a מולד after חצות.
steps.simpleTranslation: אבא, the father of רבי שמלאי, said to שמואל: Do you know the meaning of what is taught in סוד העיבור, "born before midday or born after midday"?
steps.whatsHappening: Someone tests שמואל's claim by asking him about a difficult line in a calendar ברייתא. This question sets up the next step, where we find out whether שמואל can answer it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If שמואל really has full calendar knowledge, he should know what this ברייתא means. The question works as a test of his claim from step 2. "Born" refers to the birth of the new moon, the מולד.

keyTerms.meaning: "The secret of adding," the hidden rules for calculating the calendar (adding days and months)
Was born (here, the new moon was "born": the מולד)

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ אַבָּא אֲבוּהּ דְּרַבִּי שִׂמְלַאי לִשְׁמוּאֵל:
phrases.english: Abba, the father of Rabbi Simlai, said to Shmuel:
Does the master know this matter
that is taught in the secret of adding (the calendar):

phrases.notes: "Born" means the new moon came into being, which is called the מולד.

steps.triggerLanguage: יָדַע מָר הַאי מִילְּתָא דְּתַנְיָא בְּסוֹד הָעִיבּוּר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Tests שמואל's claim from step 2 by asking about a difficult calendar source.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether שמואל knows the meaning of the ברייתא's distinction between a מולד before חצות and a מולד after חצות.

steps.title: שמואל admits he does not know, and his claim is pushed back
steps.stepSummary: שמואל says he does not know what the line means. אבא answers that if he does not know this, there are surely other things he does not know.
steps.simpleTranslation: שמואל said: No. אבא said to him: Since you do not know this, there are other things you do not know as well.
steps.whatsHappening: שמואל honestly admits that he does not know the answer. אבא uses this to reject שמואל's claim that he could fix the calendar for everyone.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The logic is simple: one gap in knowledge suggests there are other gaps. Calendar calculation needs complete knowledge, so שמואל should not set the calendar by calculation alone. This ends the challenge to שמואל's claim.
steps.whatToRemember: שמואל's claim to fix the calendar by calculation is pushed back, because he admitted he did not know a rule from סוד העיבור.

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: מִדְּהָא לָא יָדַע מָר —
phrases.english: He said to him: Since the master does not know this,

phrases.aramaic: אִיכָּא מִילֵּי אַחְרָנְיָיתָא דְּלָא יָדַע מָר.
phrases.english: there are other matters that the master does not know.

steps.triggerLanguage: מִדְּהָא לָא יָדַע מָר אִיכָּא מִילֵּי אַחְרָנְיָיתָא דְּלָא יָדַע מָר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: שמואל answers the question from step 3, and אבא uses his answer to reject the claim from step 2.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects שמואל's claim that he could fix the calendar for the entire גולה.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: שמואל does not know a rule taught in סוד העיבור, which shows that his knowledge is not complete enough to rely on.

steps.title: רבי זירא: both the night and the day must belong to the new month
steps.stepSummary: When רבי זירא went up to ארץ ישראל, he sent a message: for a day to be ראש חודש, both its night and its day must be part of the new month.
steps.simpleTranslation: When רבי זירא went up to ארץ ישראל, he sent them a message: Both the night and the day must be of the new month.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a message from רבי זירא that begins to explain the puzzling ברייתא from step 3. It states a basic rule about which day can be ראש חודש.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The rule is that ראש חודש must be new from its very start, the night. So the מולד has to happen before that night begins. This rule is the key to the ברייתא's line about a מולד before or after חצות.

keyTerms.meaning: Went up (from בבל to ארץ ישראל)

steps.whyThisMatters: This gives the starting point for understanding the ברייתא in סוד העיבור that שמואל could not explain.

phrases.aramaic: כִּי סְלֵיק רַבִּי זֵירָא, שְׁלַח לְהוּ:
phrases.english: When Rabbi Zeira went up, he sent to them:
phrases.notes: He went up from בבל to ארץ ישראל and wrote back to the חכמים in בבל.

phrases.aramaic: צָרִיךְ שֶׁיְּהֵא לַיְלָה וָיוֹם מִן הֶחָדָשׁ.
phrases.english: It is necessary that the night and the day be of the new month.

steps.triggerLanguage: כִּי סְלֵיק רַבִּי זֵירָא, שְׁלַח לְהוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins to explain the ברייתא about a מולד before or after חצות that שמואל did not know.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A day can be ראש חודש only if both its night and its day belong to the new month, meaning the מולד must happen before that night begins.

steps.title: Explaining the line about a מולד before or after midday
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא explains the line אבא asked שמואל about. If the מולד is before חצות, the moon will be seen near sunset. If it is not before חצות, it will not be seen near sunset.
steps.simpleTranslation: This is what אבא אבוה דרבי שמלאי meant: we calculate when the new moon is born. If it is born before midday, we know it will be seen close to sunset. If it is not born before midday, we know it will not be seen close to sunset.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי זירא's message from ארץ ישראל goes on to explain the puzzling line from step 3 that שמואל could not explain.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The rule depends on when the מולד happens. A מולד before חצות leaves enough of the day for the new moon to become visible by sunset. A מולד after חצות does not leave enough time, so the moon cannot be seen that evening. The word וזו ties this to the idea just mentioned in step 5.

keyTerms.meaning: Its birth: the מולד, the moment the new moon begins

steps.confusionAlert: Here חצות means the middle of the day, noon. It does not mean midnight.

phrases.aramaic: וְזוֹ שֶׁאָמַר אַבָּא אֲבוּהּ דְּרַבִּי שִׂמְלַאי:
phrases.english: And this is what Abba, the father of Rabbi Simlai, said:
phrases.notes: This is the line Abba asked שמואל about back in step 3.
"Its birth" means the new moon's מולד.

phrases.english: If it was born before midday,
it is known that it is seen
If it was not born before midday,
it is known that it is not seen

steps.triggerLanguage: וְזוֹ שֶׁאָמַר אַבָּא אֲבוּהּ דְּרַבִּי שִׂמְלַאי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Uses the idea from step 5 to explain the line from step 3 that שמואל did not know.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What does the line about a מולד before or after חצות mean?
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: A מולד before חצות means the moon will be seen near sunset. A מולד after חצות means it will not be seen near sunset.

steps.title: The practical use: catching false witnesses
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what difference this calculation makes. רב אשי answers that it is used to show that witnesses are lying.
steps.simpleTranslation: What practical difference does this make? רב אשי said: it is used to prove witnesses false.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks why we need this calculation if בית דין relies on witnesses anyway. רב אשי says it helps catch lying witnesses.
steps.deeperAnalysis: בית דין still sets ראש חודש through witnesses, so the calculation does not replace them. But if witnesses say they saw the new moon when the calculation shows it could not be seen, we know their testimony is false.

keyTerms.meaning: What practical difference does it make?

steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that calculation works together with testimony. It acts as a check on the witnesses and does not take their place.
steps.triggerLanguage: לְמַאי נָפְקָא מִינַּהּ? אָמַר רַב אָשֵׁי: לְאַכְחוֹשֵׁי סָהֲדֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks what practical use the calculation from step 6 has.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why does the calculation matter if בית דין relies on witnesses?
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: It is used to prove false witnesses wrong.

steps.title: The moon is hidden for twenty-four hours
steps.stepSummary: רבי זירא quotes רב נחמן: the moon is hidden for twenty-four hours. In בבל, six of those hours belong to the old moon and eighteen to the new. In ארץ ישראל, six belong to the new moon and eighteen to the old.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי זירא said in the name of רב נחמן: for twenty-four hours the moon is covered. For us in בבל, it is six hours of the old moon and eighteen of the new. For them in ארץ ישראל, it is six hours of the new moon and eighteen of the old.
steps.whatsHappening: A new teaching: there is a twenty-four hour gap between the last sighting of the old moon and the first sighting of the new moon.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The total hidden time is the same everywhere: twenty-four hours. What changes by location is how those hours divide around the מולד. In בבל, most of the hidden time comes after the מולד. In ארץ ישראל, most of it comes before the מולד.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַבִּי זֵירָא אָמַר רַב נַחְמָן:
phrases.english: Rabbi Zeira said that Rav Nachman said:
For twenty-four hours the moon is covered.
For us: six from the old
phrases.notes: "Us" means the people in בבל, and "them" means the people in ארץ ישראל.

phrases.english: for them: six from the new

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי זֵירָא אָמַר רַב נַחְמָן: עֶשְׂרִים וְאַרְבְּעָה שָׁעֵי מִכַּסֵּי סֵיהֲרָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds another astronomical fact about the moon, related to the timing ideas in step 6.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The moon is invisible for twenty-four hours. The split between old-moon hours and new-moon hours depends on location: 6/18 in בבל and 18/6 in ארץ ישראל.

steps.title: Again, used to catch false witnesses
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what difference the twenty-four hour rule makes. רב אשי again answers that it is used to prove witnesses false.
steps.simpleTranslation: What practical difference does this make? רב אשי said: it is used to prove witnesses false.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks the same practical question about רב נחמן's teaching and gets the same answer from רב אשי.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since the moon is hidden for a full twenty-four hours, witnesses cannot have seen both the old moon and the new moon within that time. If they say they did, their testimony is false.
steps.whatToRemember: Both astronomical rules, the מולד before or after חצות and the twenty-four hidden hours, are tools for catching lying witnesses. They do not replace testimony.

phrases.notes: Here it means witnesses who say they saw both the old and the new moon within the twenty-four hours.

steps.triggerLanguage: לְמַאי נָפְקָא מִינַּהּ? אָמַר רַב אָשֵׁי: לְאַכְחוֹשֵׁי סָהֲדֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks what practical use רב נחמן's rule from step 8 has.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why does it matter that the moon is hidden for twenty-four hours?
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: It is used to prove false witnesses wrong.

steps.title: Where do we learn that night and day must both be in the new month?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the rule from רבי זירא's message and asks for its source.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Master said: For a day to be ראש חודש, both its night and its day must be part of the new month. From where do we know this?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes back to the rule from Step 5 and asks which פסוק teaches it. This line sets up the answers that come next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Earlier the rule was only reported as a message from רבי זירא. Now the גמרא wants to know what it is based on. The idea is that the night comes first and belongs to the day that follows it.

keyTerms.meaning: "From where do we know this?": a request for the source

phrases.english: The Master said: It is necessary that there be
phrases.notes: This is the rule רבי זירא sent from ארץ ישראל in Step 5.

phrases.english: a night and a day of the new month.
From where do we know this?

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר מָר: צָרִיךְ שֶׁיְּהֵא לַיְלָה וָיוֹם מִן הֶחָדָשׁ. מְנָלַן?
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Goes back from the discussion of hours and false witnesses (Steps 8-9) to the rule in Step 5, and asks for its source.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The scriptural source for the rule that ראש חודש needs both its night and its day in the new month.

steps.title: רבי יוחנן's source: from evening to evening
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן learns the rule from the פסוק 'from evening to evening.'
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוחנן said: The source is the פסוק 'From evening to evening.'
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוחנן gives the first answer. The פסוק shows that a day runs from one evening to the next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If a day starts in the evening, the night is the first part of that day. So for a day to be fully in the new month, its night must already be in the new month too.

keyTerms.meaning: "From evening to evening": a day begins at night and runs to the next night

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the first answer to the question in Step 10.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The פסוק 'from evening to evening' shows that a day begins at evening, so the night is part of the day.

steps.title: ריש לקיש's source: until the twenty-first day at evening
steps.stepSummary: ריש לקיש learns the rule from a פסוק about eating מצה on פסח.
steps.simpleTranslation: ריש לקיש said: The source is the פסוק 'Until the twenty-first day of the month at evening.'
steps.whatsHappening: ריש לקיש gives a different source. It comes from the פסוק about eating מצה, which ends 'at evening' of the twenty-first.
steps.deeperAnalysis: He agrees with the rule but learns it from another פסוק. That פסוק shows that the holiday ends at evening and a new day begins then. This leads to the next question: does it matter which פסוק we use?

keyTerms.meaning: The twenty-first (day of ניסן, the end of פסח)

phrases.notes: שמות 12:18, about eating מצה on פסח.

steps.triggerLanguage: רֵישׁ לָקִישׁ אָמַר: ״עַד יוֹם הָאֶחָד וְעֶשְׂרִים לַחֹדֶשׁ בָּעָרֶב״
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a second answer to the same question, using a different פסוק from רבי יוחנן's.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The פסוק 'until the twenty-first day of the month at evening' shows that a day ends and a new one begins at evening.

steps.title: What difference is there between the two sources?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks whether the two sources lead to any different result.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the difference between them?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks whether it matters if we follow רבי יוחנן's פסוק or ריש לקיש's פסוק. This sets up the two answers that come next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both אמוראים agree on the rule, so the גמרא wants to know whether choosing one פסוק over the other changes any law.

keyTerms.meaning: "What is the difference between them?": the practical result of a disagreement

phrases.english: What is the difference between them?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Compares the two sources just given in Steps 11 and 12.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether the two sources lead to any different practical law.

steps.title: אביי: they only differ in how they read the פסוק
steps.stepSummary: אביי says there is no practical difference; they only disagree about which פסוק teaches the rule.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said: The only difference between them is how the פסוקים are read.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי answers that the law comes out the same either way. The only disagreement is about which פסוק is the right source.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Sometimes two אמוראים agree on the law and only argue about which פסוק it comes from. אביי says this is one of those cases, so no ruling changes.

keyTerms.meaning: How the פסוק is read and explained; a disagreement only about the source

steps.confusionAlert: Don't think אביי means the two אמוראים disagree about the law. He means they agree on the law and only argue about which פסוק it comes from.

phrases.notes: He means there is no practical difference at all, only a different way of learning the rule from the פסוק.

steps.triggerLanguage: אַבָּיֵי אָמַר: מַשְׁמָעוּת דּוֹרְשִׁין אִיכָּא בֵּינַיְיהוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the first answer to the question in Step 13.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: There is no practical difference; the two only differ in which פסוק they use.

steps.title: רבא: they differ about the time before midnight
steps.stepSummary: רבא says there is a practical difference: the hours of the night before חצות לילה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: The difference between them is midnight.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא disagrees with אביי and says there is a real difference in practice. It concerns the old moon still being seen early in the night of the thirtieth, before midnight.
steps.deeperAnalysis: According to רבי יוחנן ('from evening to evening'), the new month's night must begin at nightfall. So if the old moon is still seen even at the beginning of the night of the thirtieth, that day can no longer be sanctified as ראש חודש. According to ריש לקיש, whose source is מצה, the first half of the night is distinct, because the required time for eating מצה ends at midnight, so the night can be counted from midnight. So even if the old moon is seen at the beginning of that night, the thirtieth can still be sanctified as ראש חודש, and witnesses are pressed to say they saw the new moon.

keyTerms.meaning: Unleavened bread; eating it on the first night of פסח is required only until midnight

steps.whatToRemember: Both רבי יוחנן and ריש לקיש agree that ראש חודש needs a night and a day in the new month. אביי says they only argue about the source. רבא says they differ in practice when the old moon is still seen early in the night of the thirtieth, before midnight: for רבי יוחנן that day can no longer be ראש חודש, while ריש לקיש's פסוק lets the night count from midnight, so it can still be sanctified.

phrases.notes: He means the hours of the night before midnight; that is where the two sources lead to different results.

steps.triggerLanguage: רָבָא אָמַר: חֲצוֹת לַיְלָה אִיכָּא בֵּינַיְיהוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Disagrees with אביי's answer in Step 14 and gives a practical difference instead.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: There is a practical difference when the old moon is still seen before midnight on the night of the thirtieth. For רבי יוחנן that day can no longer be ראש חודש; ריש לקיש's פסוק about מצה lets the night count from midnight, so it can still be sanctified.

steps.title: רב נחמן: a day of doubt is pushed forward
steps.stepSummary: רבי זירא quotes רב נחמן: whenever we keep a day because of calendar doubt, we add it after the real date, not before. So we keep the 15th and 16th, but not the 14th.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי זירא said that רב נחמן said: Any day of doubt, we throw it forward. That means we keep the fifteenth and the sixteenth, but we do not keep the fourteenth.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts a new topic. It brings רב נחמן's rule about where the extra day of יום טוב goes when we are unsure of the date.
steps.deeperAnalysis: When we are not sure which day is יום טוב, we could add an extra day before it or after it. רב נחמן says we only add it after. The גמרא then spells out the result: the 15th and 16th are kept, and the 14th is not.

keyTerms.meaning: A doubt; here, uncertainty about the correct date
We throw it forward, so the extra day comes after
That is to say; it introduces what the rule means in practice
We observe, we keep (the יום טוב)

steps.confusionAlert: 'Forward' means later in time. The extra day is added after the main date (the 16th), not before it (the 14th).
steps.whyThisMatters: This is the basic idea behind why יום טוב שני in חוץ לארץ is the day after the יום טוב, not the day before.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַבִּי זֵירָא אָמַר רַב נַחְמָן:
phrases.english: Rabbi Zeira said that Rav Nachman said:

phrases.notes: He means the extra day we keep because of the doubt goes after the date, not before it.

phrases.english: that we keep the fifteenth and the sixteenth,
but the fourteenth we do not keep.
phrases.notes: These are days of the month on which a יום טוב falls, like סוכות on the 15th of תשרי.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי זֵירָא אָמַר רַב נַחְמָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic, separate from the argument between אביי and רבא about the night before חצות.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A day kept out of calendar doubt is added after the date (15th and 16th), never before it (the 14th).

steps.title: Why not also keep the fourteenth?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges רב נחמן: maybe both אב and אלול were made short months. If so, the day people count as the 14th is really the 15th, so it should be kept too.
steps.simpleTranslation: But let us also keep the fourteenth! Perhaps they made אב short and they made אלול short!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks רב נחמן's rule. It argues that the doubt can also go backward, so the 14th should be kept as well.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב נחמן assumed the doubt only pushes the date later. The גמרא points out a case that pushes it earlier: if both אב and אלול had 29 days, the real 15th would fall on the day people think is the 14th. So the doubt seems to cover the 14th too.

keyTerms.meaning: But let us also keep; the opening of a challenge
They made it short, a month of 29 days instead of 30

phrases.english: But let us also keep the fourteenth?

phrases.notes: If both months had only 29 days, the day people count as the 14th would really be the 15th.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רב נחמן's rule from step 16 that the 14th is not kept.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב נחמן's claim that the doubt only pushes forward, so the 14th is not kept.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If both אב and אלול were short, the true 15th would fall on the day counted as the 14th. So the doubt also points backward, and the 14th should be kept.
